In my opinion, it's still the best anon coin, yes. Reason is simple: Cryptonote is still the best anon-tech out there, and Monero is still the first fair-release non-scam Cryptonote coin. Solid devs, solid community, etc...

I'll also add another realization I've recently had... I used to think that Monero (or Cryptonote more generally) was just a stopgap on the way to a full zero-knowledge-proof-based coin such as the theoretical Zerocoin/cash. But there are essentially three issues with ZC that make it unworkable in practice, in my opinion: 1) The initial seed cannot be provably destroyed (thus, one can never be 100% sure that someone doesn't have keys to the entire kingdom). 2) Given that the system is fully obfuscated, observers can never look at the blockchain and count all the coins; thus no one can ever be sure that there's not some bug somewhere that's letting an attacker create and spend coins. 3) Completely obscuring all transaction amounts in all cases is actually not optimal. Users should have control. Workable financial systems need privacy, but also optional transparency. ZC doesn't provide the option. Monero's viewkeys provide a very nice practical solution for transparency.

tldr: Yes, Monero is still the best, and I think it is likely to remain so given that Zerocoin/cash is probably not realistically a long-term threat.
